description: Normative v0.5 MUSTs (the inter-agent leg, SCP #24) a human reviewer confirms are present and correctly scoped in spec/v0.5.md. NOT executable. Complements pa-001 (the v0.3/v0.4 audit set).

asserts.assert: The `to` grammar is pinned: the FIRST `#` terminates the agent-id segment and the session segment MUST match `^sess_`, so an agent id containing `#` is inexpressible in `to` (and cannot register sessions, §16.1) and the principal/session forms parse unambiguously. Absent `to` = the human inbox, unchanged; `to: human:...` is invalid in 0.5.

Submit-time destination validation is a MUST, within the submitter's account: unknown agent.id → `422 unknown_destination`; unknown session → `422`; terminal session → `410 destination_gone`; cross-account rejected identically to unknown (no existence oracle); the same validation applies RETROACTIVELY to the §13 directive `to`. Accepting an unroutable destination and silently dead-lettering is named as the false-belief failure the delivery-honesty rules exist to kill. When the sender lacks §16 visibility for the destination, the terminal-vs-unknown split MUST collapse to `422` (no session-state oracle).

Sender-side symmetry is a MUST: an addressed (or `agent.session`-bearing) submit from a principal whose own agent.id contains `#` is rejected `422 invalid_field` — a `#`-bearing id cannot participate in the inter-agent leg on either end, while its human-inbox traffic is unaffected.

`agent.session` MUST name one of the authenticated principal's OWN registered sessions (foreign/unknown → `422`; own-but-terminal → `410`); when present, the Caller's mailbox for Response delivery is that session and the Hub-attested `from` on the delivered form is session-qualified. `agent.session` and `agent.run_id` are EXCLUDED from the §8.1 idempotency identical-payload comparison.

The delivered-on-acceptance notify rule applies ONLY to the human-inbox path: an ADDRESSED notify is acked `202 { "status": "queued" }` — an ack asserting `delivered` at accept time would itself be the banned false belief — and its lifecycle IS the §14.2 delivery track. On EVERY addressed ack, of any verb, the addressed marker and misroute detector is the REQUIRED `destination` snapshot, never the `status` value.

The addressee of an addressed ask/task resolves via the §8.8 binding with its agent credential; the Hub attests the session-qualified `actor`. The resolver default for addressed messages is the ADDRESSEE (absent `allowed_resolvers`, only the `to` principal may resolve — the submitter must NOT answer its own ask, and the account's human is deliberately NOT a default resolver; the operator's recourse is the §16 kill-switch). Principal-form entries match any session of the principal; session-qualified entries match only that exact session.

When the Caller registered a session and it is LIVE at resolution time, the Hub additionally delivers the Response to that session's mailbox as a §9.8-signed `response` entry; no session, or a terminal session, falls back to the unchanged v0.4 path (§8.2 pull authoritative, §8.3 callback) with NO bounce emitted. Every channel carries the same `resolution_id`; the agent dedups on (in_reply_to, resolution_id).

When an addressed ask/task's delivery track reaches EITHER undeliverable terminal — `bounced` OR `expired` — the ask auto-resolves `cancelled` and the task `dismissed` with attested `response.actor: "system:undeliverable"` (no new resolution values), riding the same atomic first-terminal-wins CAS (a no-op returning the existing Response when already terminal).

The inter-agent leg is account-opt-in: `inter_agent.enabled` defaults FALSE and a Hub MUST NOT accept `to`-addressed submits for an account that has not opted in. Per-destination sender allowlists are REQUIRED of a conformant Hub offering the leg; an allowlist-blocked submit MUST be rejected `422 unknown_destination`, indistinguishable from a nonexistent destination. `inter_agent` requires the §14 primitive (advertising it without `ack`, including the v0.5 terminal states, is non-conformant). A 0.5 sender MUST feature-detect via §8.0 before using `to` AND apply the §8.1 ack misroute check.

The advertised `inbound.stream_max_hold_seconds` MUST be ≤ the presence freshness window — a cross-field relation the schema dialect cannot compare, discharged by the Hub's own conformance tests (dp-021).

The ack for an addressed message MUST carry the destination's current §15 reachability snapshot; when the sender lacks visibility the object MUST be exactly `{ "state": "unknown" }` with no `last_seen`. A 0.5 sender MUST treat an addressed-submit ack WITHOUT `destination` as a misroute (a pre-0.5 Hub silently routed the envelope to the human inbox), MUST surface the failure, and SHOULD cancel a misrouted ask via §8.4. Idempotent replay is run-independent: a same-key replay from a new session/run returns the original ack (original `id`, current owning-track status) and the ORIGINAL submit's session remains the bound Caller (first submit wins).

The session-scoped drain rules are pinned: `?session=` MUST be the caller's own session — foreign/unknown → `404` (indistinguishable), own-but-terminal → `410` ("re-register and continue"); a session-LESS drain returns exactly the v0.4 shape (a 0.4 consumer never sees an unknown entry shape); the v0.5 entry kinds are delivered ONLY to session-presenting drains; the §8.7 webhook remains directives-only. Session presentation on an ack affects lease attribution only, never ack authorization.

The Hub MUST strip submitter-side machinery from a delivered `message` entry (`state`, `client_ref`, any `request.callback`/`action.callback`); `from` is Hub-attested (session-qualified when the submit carried `agent.session`), the `agent` descriptor advisory. Ack keys are pinned per kind (directive `id`, message `id`, response `resolution_id`, receipt `id`) and signature-bound; the id namespaces (`dir_`/`msg_`/`res_`/`rcpt_`/`sess_`) are normative for v0.5-minted ids (pre-0.5 ids grandfathered, the Hub remaining responsible for ack-key uniqueness). Principal-addressed entries are first-claim-wins under visibility-timeout semantics; addressed messages default out of the human triage inbox but MUST remain readable/auditable by the account's authenticated human.

A merely-open SSE socket is NOT liveness evidence: an open connection MUST NOT by itself renew the session lease or presence; the Hub MUST bound each stream hold (closed with a NONZERO margin before lease expiry, ≤ the advertised hold bound) and the client's reconnect is the renewal. Stream delivery is provisional: only client-originated receipt evidence advances the delivery track — a stream-pushed, never-acked entry reverts to queued-visible and its track never left `queued`. Long-poll drain remains the conformance floor.

The resolve binding validates `resolution` against the verb and `value` against the request block (`value` REQUIRED iff `answered`, forbidden otherwise; `checklist` task-only) with `422 invalid_field`, applies the §7 atomic CAS (a resolve after a terminal returns `409 already_terminal` with the existing outcome), and emits the §6 Response through every configured channel — push, pull, and the §8.7 `response` entry for a live submitting session.

Each v0.5 entry kind carries a detached signature the consumer MUST verify before acting — §9.7's discipline applied to three new contexts: RFC 8785 JCS, the MA2H-Signature header, digests RECOMPUTED by the verifier from the payload it received (never trusted from the wire) over fixed-key wrappers, per-delivery re-signing with a fresh `t`/`jti`, the ±window `t` check and `jti` cache (TTL ≥ window), and key rotation with overlap. The message content digest binds exactly the present fields among type/title/body/priority/tags/context/request/action/sensitive (`type` and `sensitive` bound; `created_at`/`expires_at`/`agent`/`idempotency_key` advisory-unbound); the response context replaces `callback_url` with `to` (reconstructed from the verifier's own drain identity; `id` always equals `in_reply_to`; `resolved_at` is JSON null when the response detail is absent); the receipt digest is over the fixed six-key wrapper with absent members as null, binding the receipt's ack-key `id`.

v0.5 is additive and non-breaking: every v0.3/v0.4 leg is byte-for-byte unchanged, a pre-0.5 agent never presents a session and never sees the new entry kinds, and the push-parity threshold stays anchored at the signature-break minor (3). The two deliberate behavior changes are named: (1) a 0.5 Hub rejects (`422`/`410`) directive submissions to unknown/terminal destinations a 0.4 Hub silently dead-lettered; (2) a 0.5 sender MUST feature-detect before using `to` and MUST treat an addressed ack lacking `destination` as a misroute.

The §13.4 duties apply WHOLESALE to `message` entries, with two v0.5 amendments: (1) the addressee check extends to the session qualifier — the recipient MUST confirm `to`'s principal is itself AND, when session-qualified, that the named session is its own CURRENT session (a validly-signed entry for a prior session is refused); (2) before ACTING on an addressed ask/task the agent MUST evaluate an explicit, deployment-declared authorization policy for which `from` principals may ask/task it — never an implicit runtime default. `response`/`receipt` entries are solicited outcomes: verification, dedup, ack — not command surface.

The lateral-movement threat model is closed in layers, NONE optional: the account opts in (`inter_agent.enabled` default false); the Hub MUST support per-destination sender allowlists (blocked → collapsed `422`, no enumeration oracle); the recipient MUST act only under an explicit deployment-declared policy; fleet traffic MUST remain human-auditable. The trust boundary is unchanged — the account: cross-account addressing is rejected as unknown and the leg creates no cross-account path.

The delivery-honesty terminals are pinned: `expired` MUST mean never delivered (mailbox track: never drained; response track: retention passed short of `delivered-to-agent`), and once `delivered`, later resolution-track expiry never rewrites the delivery track. `bounced` covers EVERY un-acked session-addressed command entry on session death — including drained-but-unacked (receipt `prior` preserving `queued` = never-seen vs `delivered` = seen-then-orphaned) — plus the principal-addressed retention orphan (bounced, `prior: "delivered"`, `session` naming the last claimant); `response`/`receipt` entries NEVER bounce; delivery-track expiry emits no receipt in v0.5 (`receipt.event` carries only `bounced`).

Presence extends per session from the session's client-originated renewal events, evaluated against the same freshness window, and derivation is SPLIT per consumption capability: addressed-message reachability derives from session-bearing activity ONLY (a destination whose only consumer drains session-less MUST NOT read `online` there), while v0.4 directive presence keeps the any-authenticated-drain derivation. The truthfulness rule is a MUST: never `online` absent qualifying client-originated activity in the window; never a delivery-track advance absent client-originated receipt evidence (drain response, ack, or §9.4-verified webhook 2xx) — a server-originated stream push never counts; optimistic reporting is non-conformant.

Sessions add NO new credentials: a session id is not a secret and is operable only by the registering principal — with the single §16.4 exception that the account's authenticated HUMAN may close any account session (the audited kill-switch, whose bounce then unblocks waiting senders). The lease renews only on client-originated activity naming the session; `active → closed | expired` are terminal and immutable (first-terminal-wins); on either terminal the Hub MUST apply the §14.2 bounce rules to un-acked session-addressed command mail. Own-session visibility is unconditional; another principal's session id MUST be indistinguishable from unknown; cross-account never. The known same-credential limitation (sessions of one principal can impersonate each other's session address) is documented, with per-session derived tokens as roadmap.

Hub durability extends to the inter-agent leg: a restart MUST NOT lose any un-acked mailbox entry of ANY kind (message/response/receipt entries carry the same drainable-until-acked-or-terminal guarantee as directives), any ACTIVE session lease (a session reaches `closed`/`expired` only by its two defined transitions — a restart silently forgetting a live lease would fire the bounce rules as an undocumented third terminal path), or any pending bounce obligation (the §14.2 transitions and their auto-resolutions re-applied after restart while incomplete).
